page.layout: One text column with margin notes in the left margin. Running head at the top, printed page number at the top left. Heading "CAPITIS VI." and "SECTIO II." in the column. Gathering signature "K" at the foot.

main_text.p: noftra, quatenus per illam sanguine Christi in cruce effuso afperguntur.

Ephef. 5. 2. Christus dilexit nos, & tradidit semetipsum pro nobis oblationem, & victimam Deo in odorem bonae fragrantiae. Unde etiam ἱλασμὸς sive ἱλαστήριον noftrum appellatur, Rom. 3.25. & 1. Joh. 2.2. Ut intelligamus, cum oblatione corporis sui Deum nobis ob peccata vere offensum placasse.

Concludo igitur, Iesum Christum summum Pontificem nostrum semetipsum pro nobis victimam Deo offerendo, & pro nobis intercedendo, iram Dei vere nobis placasse, favorem ejus reconciliasse, non vero tantum nos placatos declarasse.
main_text.head: CAPITIS VI.
SECTIO II.
main_text.p: Qui ideo semetipsum obtulit Deo in mortem, non modo ut annuntiatae salutis viam ostenderet[?], confirmaret, & significaret, sed principaliter, ut peccata propter eum nobis remitti possent: atq; ita justitia, quae coram Deo nobis est confistendum, instauraretur, is professio[?] ideo mortuum dici potest, ut morte sua pro pecca-2. Argum. Finis mortis Christi Remissio peccatorum & justitia. Propositio.

page.notes: Printed page number and running head are at the top. The first line of the page continues the previous paragraph. The left margin notes "2. Argum.", "Finis mortis Christi Remissio peccatorum & justitia." and "Propositio." are placed at the start of the paragraph beginning "Qui ideo". Doubtful readings: "ostenderet" (the ligature is unclear), "professio" (the word is hard to read), and the Greek ἱλασμὸς sive ἱλαστήριον, which I copied from the scan and have not verified letter by letter. The paragraph ends with the hyphenated "pecca-" at the bottom of the page, which continues on the next page. The Ephesians reference is printed as "Ephef." with the numbers as shown.
